chapter: Closing: recent career, family and travel
title: Tribute to the first all-Black USO troupe
summary: On 13 May they are to receive a tribute at the 369th Regiment Armory; only he and Julia Gardner survive from the troupe.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Well, I think that's pretty good. If you think of anything else that we've omitted of importance, well, then, just let me know, and that can be added onto the transcript...
[PAUSE]
You're saying on the 13th of April...
The 13th of May. They're giving me a tribute.
Who are they?

Dick Campbell of the sickle cell organization. There will be a lot of people there. I'll tell you much more about it before you leave. We are the only two living people from the original first all-Black USO troupe. You must remember, during the time that they sent colored acts over there for the Black troops over there, that was an experiment. So they went on to the USO troupes; prior to that, they weren't using them at all.
This was when you went down to the Caribbean Islands.
The Second World War, yeah. We were supposed
Ramirez - 213
to go all over Europe, but I came back here and I joined... I think I joined Kirby's band after that. But anyway, Julia Gardner and myself are the only two living ones...
Julia Gardner?
Julia Gardner. She plays accordion.
Yes, I remember.
It was Kenneth Spencer, myself, Willie Bryant, Betty Logan, and Julia Gardner. And so, they're giving us a tribute at the 369th Regiment Armory on the 13th of May.
Does she still play?
Yeah, she's still playing around. Very well, too.
Yeah, I heard her a lot in ...(?)., and I thought she was very good.
Yeah, she's one of the very good female accordionists.
Well, something could have been done with it.
Yeah, and... Well...
Enough of that.
